mn140:14.4: The earth, water, fire, and air element passages (sections 14–17) parallel the fuller treatment in Sutta 28, where the same four elements are explained at greater length, including their disturbance on a cosmic scale.
mn140:18.5: ‘Void, an opening, unfilled by flesh or blood’ describes the hollow bodily cavities and passages, distinguishing space in oneself from the solid, liquid, hot, and mobile elements.
mn140:21.2: That is, the base consisting of infinite space, the first of the four formless attainments.
mn140:22.11: This means that he does not cling to anything in any world, to any state of existence—not even to the most refined formless heavens.
mn140:22.12: Fear and agitation arise from craving and clinging; without them there is no agitation, and Nibbāna is attained personally, here and now.
mn140:24.5: ‘Become cool’ is a description of Nibbāna, parallel to the lamp ‘going out’ in the following simile.
mn140:31.4: Muni (‘sage’) has the double sense of ‘one who is silent’ (in the Dhamma, one who does not construe anything as self) and ‘one who has wisdom’; cf. Sutta 131.
mn140:35.2: A cow rushing after her calf.
